title: finding(types): `RecordHighlightsComponentProps.layout` offers a third value `grid` the spec enum refuses — `tsc` green, publish RED
body:
Found while surveying `layout` occurrences for objectui#9040 (the neighbouring
key on the neighbouring interface, in the same file). Different interface,
different key, opposite half of the file — so it is filed rather than carried on
that branch.

`packages/types/src/record-components.ts`:

```ts
export interface RecordHighlightsComponentProps {
  /** Layout mode for highlights display */
  layout?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' | 'grid';   // three values
}
```

`@objectstack/spec` declares two.

## Measured, on the installed pin (17.4.0), against controls

Reading `RecordHighlightsProps`'s own shape rather than transcribing anything:

```
shape keys        : ["aria","fields","layout"]
layout member     : default -> enum ["horizontal","vertical"]
```

The parse probes, one instrument, one loop, every row with `fields: ['name']`
so the document is otherwise valid:

```
{ layout: 'horizontal' }    GREEN
{ layout: 'vertical' }      GREEN
{ layout: 'grid' }          RED   invalid_value at `layout`
{ layout: 'zzzNonsense' }   RED   invalid_value at `layout`     <- CONTROL
{ }  (key omitted)          GREEN                               <- CONTROL
```

Both controls fired as they should: an arbitrary value is refused with the SAME
code as `grid`, so `grid` is not special-cased, and omitting the key parses
green, so the schema is not refusing everything.

## Why it matters

A TypeScript author writes `layout: 'grid'` on a `record:highlights` block,
`tsc` is green, and the contract refuses the document at publish with
`invalid_value`. That is the same class of trap as objectui#8604 (a body-wide
`columns` typed `number` against a string enum) and objectui#9040 item 1 (the
retired `layout` one interface up): the published TypeScript face offers a value
the only layer that matters rejects.

Two more layers already agree with the spec and not with this declaration:

- `@object-ui/plugin-detail`'s registry manifest publishes
  `{ name: 'layout', type: 'enum', enum: ['horizontal', 'vertical'] }` — two
  values, not three.
- The comment directly above that registration states that
  `RecordHighlightsProps` has exactly three top-level keys and cites a control
  measured on 17.2.0.

So `grid` appears to be live on exactly one layer: this published type.

## Direction, if it is taken

Contract-first (Commandment #0.1) points at narrowing the declaration to the
contract's two values rather than widening anything. ⚠️ That is a NARROWING of a
published type: a consumer that wrote `grid` stops compiling, so it needs the
in-repo consumer survey and the FROM/TO changeset that a narrowing carries, the
same shape objectui#8604 used. I did not run that survey — this card is the
measurement, not the plan.

⛔ Not claimed, ⛔ not graded — labels, `domain:*` and priority are triage's.

Refs: objectui#9040 (where this was found; the sibling interface's top level) ·
objectui#8604 (the same class, one interface over) · objectui#3818 (the
`record:details` `layout` retirement). Deduped before filing: a REST sweep of
400 `package: types` cards in both states, plus one targeted semantic search, and that
returned no card on this key — the search was live, it returned objectui#9040
and objectui#3818 as on-topic neighbours.

Reported by an ObjectStack dev agent seat; session reference
`https://claude.ai/code/session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ` (written as prose
because an attribution footer does not survive issue creation).
